audit.why: 52.94% over 1749 games at 7/10. Annie's stocked stun plus Tibbers punishes the dive, but Zed's 900-range Razor Shuriken means she loses every exchange she cannot reach, and one unstacked moment at 6 ends her.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[].side read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Zed/Skill/Skill against win[]'s Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Zed/Annie.
audit.why: Four rows disagreed, and the level 6 row was inverted between layers — the full layer gave 6 to Zed while the content layer gave it to Annie and gave first item to Zed. win[] matches packet.levelChart.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side realigned to the win[] chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places call Shadow Slash his ranged poke ('Poke with Shadow Slash from max range', 'Zed's Shadow Slash chip poke keeps him safe from your short stun range', 'punishing any Shadow Slash poke'). Death Mark's untargetability was never mentioned. mid calls the mark an execute.
audit.why: Shadow Slash is 290 range — shorter than Annie's 625 Q, so it cannot poke her from outside her stun radius. The ranged poke is Razor Shuriken at 900. Death Mark makes Zed untargetable during the dash, so a stun spent on the entry is wasted; it must be held for his arrival. And Death Mark repeats a portion of damage already dealt, which is not an execute.
audit.corrected: Poke references moved to Razor Shuriken with its 900 range; the untargetable window written into the cooldown and do's; the execute wording removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Death Mark a fifteen-second cooldown, and Living Shadow — the cooldown that actually governs lane — was never given a number.
audit.why: Death Mark is 120/110/100s, eight times the stated figure. Living Shadow is 20/19/18/17/16s and is the real green light: a Zed with no shadow cannot leave Annie's radius.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] says the combo 'deletes his shadow-clone HP bar'.
audit.why: Living Shadow's shadow is not a damageable unit with a health bar — it is a position marker Zed can swap to. Nothing about it can be deleted.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around swapping out rather than a phantom health bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave used the generic 'every assassin timer in the game' template.
audit.why: Zed IS the assassin in question, so the line says nothing. His concrete punish is shoving with Razor Shuriken and holding Living Shadow for the step-up.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. It governs your forward steps. - E Molten Shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Zed Death Mark: 120s at rank 1 — he is untargetable through the dash, so hold the stun for his arrival, never the entry. - Living Shadow is the lane cooldown at 20s: with the shadow spent he has no exit from your radius. Shadow Slash is 5s.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: He is untargetable through the dash — hold the stun until he lands, then spend everything at once.

edits.before: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — that is a 120-second open door.

edits.before: That’s Zed’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Living Shadow is 20s — shove without it tracked and he picks the fight.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry through one button — Flash-Tibbers once Living Shadow is spent, because then he has no exit from your radius.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — every assassin timer in the game points at that picture. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — Zed shoves it back with Razor Shuriken and holds the shadow for your step-up. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.

edits.before: Your full stun combo (Q-W into E) deletes his shadow-clone HP bar before he can react, so once you have three points up, punishing any Shadow Slash poke he throws out becomes a near-guaranteed kill window.
edits.after: Your full stun combo lands before he can swap back to his shadow, so once three abilities are up, punishing a Razor Shuriken he threw with Living Shadow already spent is a near-guaranteed kill window.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 favor neither side clearly — Zed's Shadow Slash chip poke keeps him safe from your short stun range, and you don't have the combo burst yet to punish his aggression, so it's mostly a wave-management stalemate.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 favor neither side clearly — Zed chips you with Razor Shuriken from 900 range while standing outside your 625 stun, and you lack the combo burst to punish it, so it stays a wave-management stalemate.

edits.before: From level 3 you get dangerous — a full E-Q-W stun chains long enough to dump your whole rotation on him before his shadow-swap saves him, and he simply cannot contest that trade until level 6. The instant Death Mark comes online he flips the script hard: dash in with a shadow, tag you, swap back, and the delayed mark execute can burst you down before Tibbers even lands, making his level 6 spike the scariest window in the whole matchup.
edits.after: From level 3 you get dangerous — a stocked stun buys long enough to dump your whole rotation before the shadow-swap saves him, and he cannot contest that trade until level 6. The instant Death Mark comes online he flips it: untargetable on the dash, marked, swapped back, and the mark repeating his damage three seconds later can kill you before Tibbers lands, making 6 the scariest window in the matchup.

edits.before: Poke with Shadow Slash from max range without ever entering your stun radius
edits.after: Poke with Razor Shuriken from 900 range, never entering your stun radius

edits.before: Hold Tibbers as an emergency block against his Death Mark burst
edits.after: Hold the stun for where Death Mark lands — the dash itself is untargetable

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged "Death Mark's" in whys[4] as a probable wrong name — that is a false positive, Death Mark is correct. The real name error is the opposite direction: Shadow Slash (290 range) was written three times as Zed's long-range poke where Razor Shuriken (900) was meant, which reverses the spacing advice a reader acts on. Death Mark's cooldown was stated as fifteen seconds against a real 120s.
